messages:
acme-corp-support: hey team, we're seeing duplicate completions after a client reconnect. customer says they get two full responses sometimes and were billed twice. repro steps attached below. urgent, billing impact.

Alyssa: thanks, can you paste the minimal repro? do they use streaming sse or chunked websocket?

acme-corp-support: SSE. customer uses browser EventSource. flow: open stream -> partial tokens arrive -> network blip -> reconnects immediately -> new full completion arrives. sometimes old partial continues then second full generation appended. billing shows 2x token counts.

Raj: interesting. do they include any idempotency or resume token on reconnect?

acme-corp-support: no, browser just reopens EventSource to same endpoint. no client id header or request-id.

Samir: ok probable cause: our streaming path doesn't universally mark in-flight requests with a stable generation id unless client sends one. on reconnect we may treat it as a fresh request and re-run model. if the client then also receives the tail of the previous stream (delayed), they see duplicates.

Alyssa: can we get their original request payload (headers + body) and the server side logs for that thread id? ask them to redact PII but include request timestamps.

acme-corp-support: pasted minimal payload from customer (redacted):

```
GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-large HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Client-App: acme-web-1
```

Body: json with prompt + stop tokens. no client-generated idempotency-key.

Raj: thanks. two-pronged mitigation: 1) client quick fix: include idempotency token per logical request (uuid) and server will dedupe executions; 2) server-side: improve resume semantics to attach a stable generation id to the in-flight stream events so reconnects can reconcile and dedupe. both are doable.

Julia: for immediate customer relief, suggest they add a cheap client-side de-dupe: ignore a new full completion if within 5s of last partial and identical leading tokens. not perfect but buys time. also suggest exponential reconnect backoff so they don't immediately re-trigger generation.

acme-corp-support: customer asked for a non-breaking server config toggle if we can enable dedupe on their account while we build a full fix. is that possible?

Samir: we have a per-customer middleware flag in runtime to enable "strict-stream-ids" for new streams. it will generate a server-side stream_generation_id and emit an initial control event like: `event: stream_meta\ndata: {"gen_id":"abc123"}`. client can store gen_id and send on reconnect as `X-Resume-Gen: abc123`. if reconnect lacks gen_id, runtime will fallback to default behavior. enabling for a single tenant is feasible but requires config + short deploy.

Raj: operational note: we need to ensure billing dedupe is aligned. generating gen_id doesn't stop re-execution if client reconnects without it. we'd need dedupe at billing layer keyed by gen_id+customer to avoid double charge during the enforcement window. that change touches billing pipeline.

Alyssa: can eng estimate time to toggle and patch billing dedupe? customer wants timeline.

Samir: infra + runtime: small flag flip + minor logging -> ~1-2 business days to test and deploy. billing dedupe: needs schema change to attach stream_gen to token-usage events and a dedupe pass -> ~3-4 days. can do a targeted opt-in rollout while we ship full client guidance.

acme-corp-support: customer reply: they can ship client idempotency quickly themselves (they're engineering heavy) but asked if we can provide exact header names and sample code.

Alyssa: I'll paste recommended client snippet for EventSource reconnect handling. short and pragmatic.

Alyssa: "Suggested client pattern (browser)":

```
// 1) create a stable request id for each logical generation
const reqId = crypto.randomUUID();
let es = new EventSource(`/v1/stream?model=redwood-large`, { headers: { 'X-Request-Id': reqId } });

es.onmessage = (e) => { /* handle partial token */ };
es.onerror = () => {
  // exponential backoff reconnect, include same X-Request-Id
  setTimeout(() => { es = new EventSource(`/v1/stream?model=redwood-large`, { headers: { 'X-Request-Id': reqId } }); }, backoffMs);
};
```

Alyssa: this makes the server able to dedupe if we flip strict-stream-ids on.

Julia: also recommend client capture message event IDs (if we emit them) and drop duplicates by comparing first 32 tokens or an event id.

acme-corp-support: customer asks: why do we sometimes get a trailing partial from the previous run after reconnect? they said the browser showed partial tokens then blank, then second full completion appended.

Raj: two reasons: 1) network reorder / delayed SSE segments — the connection may have buffered partials; 2) our runtime may continue generating for a short tail if the TCP teardown wasn't fully acknowledged. combined with immediate reconnect, client sees both tails.

Samir: small reproducible test we ran in staging: spawn a stream, delay TCP FIN, trigger reconnect with same prompt and no idempotency -> two generations observed by client. we can attach logs.

acme-corp-support: attaching staging logs and a timeline. customer ok with trying the client idempotency patch first.

Alyssa: next steps: 1) ask customer to add X-Request-Id header and enable exponential backoff; 2) we will enable strict-stream-ids for their tenant temporarily (pending deploy) and notify when billing dedupe is ready; 3) eng will open an internal ticket to scope billing dedupe work.

Samir: I'll open ENG-RUNTIME ticket and include the staging repro, log snippets, and suggested server meta event API. tagging @Raj for billing follow-up.

IncidentBot: Ticket ENG-RUNTIME-1427 created by Samir: "streaming: per-tenant stream_gen ids + billing dedupe". link: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENG-RUNTIME-1427

Raj: created BILLING-984 to track dedupe work, linking ENG-RUNTIME-1427.

acme-corp-support: customer confirmed they'll patch client tonight and report back. says billing hit is small but wants us to confirm dedupe timeline.

Alyssa: I'll follow up with ETA once eng gives schedule. thanks all. :heart:
